analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. Changed head ranges are 404-413 (outside the supplied units) and 1095-1115, which I examined. No code or enforcement paths changed, so no security control was modified in this PR.

The 1095-1115 addition documents segmented paged KV admission. It describes parking free 64 MiB segments per pool, capped at min(2 GiB, slot grant/8), outside the grant, floor and ledger charge. Segments are reinstalled for the next admission of the same size class. New segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages (cbv2ZeroFilledPages). Parked backing is dropped on refused admission, a process-wide release request, or after 30 s idle. The proactive allocator sweep and the kill switches DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0 and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0 are described.

Relevant threats are T-028 (residual GPU/KV data) and T-041. The doc describes retained, uncharged KV segments reinstalled for a later request. It does not say whether parked segments are zeroed or overwritten before reuse across requests or tenants. Zero-fill-on-demand applies to new segments only. That is an unverified contract in code outside the supplied evidence, so I record it rather than raise a finding. Reuse stays within the same provider process, and T-028 already treats in-process GPU residue as an accepted or known residual. The uncharged parked memory is bounded and released on pressure, so no clear DoS regression is evidenced.

The doc text at 802-1633 is largely pre-existing context. It makes no new security claims that contradict the canonical threat model, and I did not review the implementing Swift code for the paged-segment and reclaim behavior. A later pass should confirm that the parked-segment reinstall path does not expose prior-request KV contents, and that the uncharged accounting cannot cause over-commitment. The truncated patch excerpt and the unsupplied lines 404-413 are coverage limits.
